facts.text: The entry class is Environment(Base), the Gymnasium environment class defined in environment.py
ACTIONS is the eight-button tuple (Down, Left, Right, Up, A, B, Start, Select), so the discrete action index runs from 0 to 7
The observation space is Box(low=0, high=255, dtype=np.uint8, shape=obs_size), where obs_size is the screen rows//2 and columns//2 plus four channels when use_screen_memory is true
The observation concatenates the downsampled screen with a fixed window of the per-map memory channel
reset has the signature reset(self, seed=None, options=None, max_episode_steps=20480, reward_scale=4.0) and its docstring says seeding is NOT supported
The first reset loads the first saved state; later resets do not reload it (the load happens only when reset_count == 0)
The default save state is current_state/Bulbasaur.state when state_path is None
step has the signature step(self, action, fast_video=True) and sends ACTIONS[action] to the emulator
One step runs the emulator for frame_skip=24 frames and releases the button after 8 frames
self.time is incremented by one at every step
done is True when self.time >= self.max_episode_steps
step returns (observation, reward, done, done, info): the same done bool fills terminated and truncated
The reward is the difference between the current cumulative reward_scale-scaled reward and the previous one; the first step returns 0
make_env hardcodes the ROM path to pokemon_red.gb in the working directory
The package requires the pyboy, gymnasium and numpy packages
The state files are found under pokegym/current_state/
The README instructs the user to copy pokemon_red.gb into the training directory

determinism.notes: the upstream reset ignores its seed (environment.py:618-619) and reloads the first save state only on the first reset (environment.py:620-621), so a seed does not make a trajectory repeatable; no determinism is claimed

gaps: the model is the Pokemon Red game running on the PyBoy Game Boy emulator: no physical device, forces, contacts, actuators or sensors are modelled (fidelity F0, no dynamics)

the package's fake backend is a pure Python stand-in with the real 8-button action space but a synthetic 8x8x4 uint8 observation; it does not emulate the ROM, the game's reward or the upstream 72x80x4 uint8 screen array (environment.py:137-149), and it was never compared with the upstream environment

no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0; one step advances the emulator 24 frames (pyboy_binding.py:71-88) but the clone states no frame duration, so timestep_ms is 0 and ticks are not converted to seconds
reset is partial: the first reset loads the first save state, later resets keep the emulator's current game state (environment.py:620-621)
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment has save_state/load_first_state helpers but no get_state/set_state pair the bridge could use
the ROM (pokemon_red.gb) and the emulator are not in the clone, so the upstream environment was never run here

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
